details_checked: Candidate makes PostgreSQL ai_jobs authoritative, removes long LLM work from API request lifecycles, and gives a durable 202/job-status/event lifecycle resilient to disconnects and process restarts.

Candidate specifies at-least-once external execution, atomic SKIP LOCKED claims, leases, heartbeats, conditional completion, stale-result discard, bounded retry, DLQ, and controlled requeue rather than exactly-once claims.
Candidate specifies replica-shared global/provider/model/task/tenant/user controls, weighted interactive preference with a 25% non-interactive floor, and a no-retry-multiplication refactor.
Candidate covers task-aware approved routing, route snapshots, circuit breaker state, failure classification, bounded approved fallback, and a data/residency trust-boundary prohibition.
Candidate labels bootstrap topology and capacity values as test inputs, gives a quota-based concurrency formula, and has evidence-based worker/broker/self-hosting triggers.

Candidate includes additive migration compatibility, exclusive legacy/new engine routing, flags, drain/rollback/requeue procedures, stop conditions, runbooks, and non-destructive schema rollback posture.
Candidate provides safe observability dimensions, no-content logging boundaries, SLOs, alerts, failure injection, load gates, quality gates, reconciliation, and explicit retained unknowns.
Candidate assesses A-E and all specified hybrids, including B plus advisory LISTEN/NOTIFY, B-now/C-later, A-then-B, and deferred D-plus-E.
implementation_options: A retained only for immediate hardening and baseline evidence, not target architecture.
B adopted as a PostgreSQL-backed durable ai_jobs and scalable asynchronous worker system.
C deferred behind measured PostgreSQL limits and transactional-outbox requirements.
D adopted as application-owned routing, circuit, evaluation, and approved fallback policy.
E rejected for current scale except independently proven regulatory or sustained-utilization contingency.
Selected hybrid is B+D, delivered through A then B and retaining B-now/C-later plus advisory LISTEN/NOTIFY.
proposed_artifact: Approved candidate v0: a PostgreSQL-first durable AI job architecture with asynchronous scalable workers and application-owned task-aware provider routing. It moves interactive LLM execution out of API lifecycles; uses idempotent job admission, SKIP LOCKED claims, expiring leases, conditional provenance-aware commits, durable status/events, shared multi-dimensional admission, weighted fairness, bounded retry/DLQ, route circuit breaking, and only equivalently approved fallback. It begins with additive schema and feature-flagged canary rollout, preserves the legacy engine during compatibility transition through exclusive ownership, includes operational rollback/reconciliation/runbooks, and defers broker/self-hosted inference decisions to defined load, database, contractual, security, and operational evidence.
requirements_covered: Responsive UX: accepted work returns durable job identity within the stated admission targets and durable retrieval survives reconnect/restart.
Durable processing: leases, retries with jitter, dead-letter visibility, idempotency, stale/lost-lease rejection, and at-least-once semantics are explicit.
Controlled concurrency and fairness: global/provider/model/task/tenant/user limits, shared budgets, interactive preference, and guaranteed background service are specified.
Provider resilience: classified failures, route circuit breaker, non-multiplying retries, and approval-gated fallback are specified.
Performance efficiency: exact reuse and bounded prompts/tokens remain; final-decision semantic caching is prohibited without correctness proof.
Proportionate topology: bootstrap deployment and explicit triggers for more workers, broker, providers, and self-hosting are supplied.
Quantitative verification: bootstrap assumptions, SLOs, safe dashboards/alerts, load testing, fault injection, and pass/fail gates are supplied.
Operational safety: additive migration, compatibility discriminator, feature flags, rollback, draining, requeue, stop conditions, and runbooks are supplied.
Cost/security: shared cross-replica budgets, safe observability, retained redaction/host controls, and residency-safe fallback are supplied.
Complete option ledger: option families A-E and relevant hybrids include retain/defer/reject rationale, dependencies, risks, and unknowns.
summary: APPROVE. Candidate v0 is a proportionate, implementation-ready B+D decision with a complete PostgreSQL-first lifecycle, measurable release gates, controlled resilience, rollback safety, and an evidence-triggered path to additional infrastructure.
